queue.brief: Three instrument lies, one file class. (1) `filmstrip.mjs --scene night` pins t=1230 s, which is day 22.4 hour ~14.7 — the night preset is a day strip; re-pin it to a real night instant (a mid-night hour on a whole day, chosen by the same rule the other presets use) and say in the file how the number was derived. (2) `runlog.mjs` grades a Harness brief 'no-ship' because srcChanged is false — #38 shipped and the dashboard says it failed; make the verdict read the brief's kind so a harness iteration that committed and logged is 'shipped' without source movement (a harness brief that DID touch courtyard.html should still be flagged). (3) A worker that ran >30 s with tokens and exited non-zero currently retires its brief as 'failed'; decide (and document in run-loop.sh) whether it is re-issued once or retired — the cheap, honest rule is one retry, then retire with the rc in the row.
queue.successLooksLike: The night filmstrip shows lit windows and lamp pools; `runlog.mjs` re-run over RUNLOG.jsonl reads #38 as shipped and no other row changes; a simulated rc=1 worker with tokens>0 is handled by the documented rule.
queue.avoid: Do not touch courtyard.html. Do not re-grade any row other than harness rows.

queue.brief: The swans carry no behaviour — `updateSwans` gives each a `ph` and a wander target and nothing else, they are announced as 'a pair' but pick targets independently, and #42's naming can only say 'a swan'. Give them states the way ducks have `swimming`: a pair that holds together (the second swan targets within a few cells of the first), an UPEND (tail up, head under, a few seconds, drawn as the body tilted with no neck) and a PREEN at rest near the bank, each a state the draw reads and `personName`/`livingAt` can say ('a swan, upended', 'a swan, preening'). Rates so that in a thirty-second look at the river you usually see one of them doing something.
queue.successLooksLike: Over ten seeds × one day the pair's mean separation is a few cells not twenty; each swan spends a measurable share of the day upended or preening; the sill names both states; motion gate clean.
queue.avoid: Do not add swans (two is the pair). Any new R() draw reshuffles the world — read the census for collapse, not delta.

queue.brief: Winter has no snow. The year has nine readers and a viewer who lands in February sees turned earth, bare trees and a skinned basin — the sky still rains. When a shower fires with `greyF()` high enough (warmth near midwinter), it falls as SNOW: slow drifting flakes instead of drops, and a `snowCover` scalar — rate-capped, per-cell variance via `hash(x, y+k)` like `fountainIce`, grain-matched to how each region is addressed — that whitens the cached ground (lawn, paving, plots), sits on roofs and awnings in the draw pass (never in `buildVolumes`), and melts over the days after as warmth climbs. It must be EXACTLY zero at SEASON_START (the anchor) by the algebra, so the summer town is byte-identical; it must not step (the cached layer buckets a quarter-hour — see the #39 law); and rain arriving on lying snow should thin it. Advertise it: one ticker line the first time it settles.
queue.successLooksLike: A midwinter shot reads as winter from the wide view: white ground with dark paths worn through it, white roof edges, flakes instead of drops. `probes/`-style year fold shows cover 0 from spring to autumn, rising in the weeks around phase 0, max step per frame under a visible threshold; noon-at-anchor frame diff vs HEAD is 0.000; perf within noise.
queue.avoid: Do not add a season or change SEASON_LEN. Do not make snow a boolean switch — it is a 0..1 like rainFall. Do not let footfall/desire-path wear interact with it this iteration; that is a follow-on cue.

queue.brief: The east half has no night: `eastOpen()` is `daylight > 0.16`, so after dark nobody crosses the bridge, and the river under `nightF` is noon water under a blue multiply while the four plaza `LAMPS` throw pools on stone and nothing on the water. Connect the night to the river: the lamps and the moon put light ON the water — a broken reflection in `drawRiverFlow` that drifts with the current, its brightness off `nightF` and the moon's height, put out by `cloudCover` like the stars are — and extend `spawnEastAgent` so that during the tap's hours (`tapOpen()`) ONE stop stays open after dark: the quay rail / parapet (`byTheWater()`), a walker who stands and looks at the lit water, then leaves the way they came. The walk is short from the quay head, so this is priced.
queue.successLooksLike: A 22.00 shot of the river shows lamp and moon reflections on the water where HEAD shows flat dark; over a night someone stands at the rail or parapet a measurable fraction of the tap's hours; the noon frame is byte-identical to HEAD; the east census counts at the anchor do not collapse.
queue.avoid: Do not open the plaza bench, fountain or church green after dark — one stop. Do not add an arrival source; widen eastOpen for that stop only. Keep the moon reflection off when the moon is below the horizon.

queue.brief: The evening door has custom from nowhere: `spawnTapAgent` rolls its own arrivals and nothing else in the town sends anybody there. Connect it: when the summer concert strikes (`bandEnd`, the audience's `a.leaveAt`), a share of the audience walks to the door instead of home, so on a concert night the pavement fills within the walk time; on a market day the last stallholder and the sweeper's opposite number call in. While there, fix c65: `scarcity()` reads `agents.length` and the tap crowd is inside it, so a full pavement damps the three night arrival RATES that POP_FLOOR lifts — scarcity must read a population the tap crowd is not part of. And assert c68: `BAND_DUSK` is a hand-computed clearance between the strike ramp and `eastOpen()`; add the check to `probes/bandstand-year.mjs` so moving BAND_DOWN/BAND_LEN/leaveAt fails a probe instead of emptying the green in one frame.
queue.successLooksLike: Folded over ten summer days, the door's occupancy in the hour after bandEnd on concert nights is measurably above ordinary nights, and the walkers who fill it came from BAND_SLOTS (same ids via __entities). scarcity() with four tap agents present equals scarcity() with none. The bandstand probe asserts the clearance.
queue.avoid: Do not add TAP_SLOTS (four; the pavement holds four at 0.9 cells). Price the walk: the bandstand-to-door trip is long — if it exceeds the tap's remaining hours on a winter concert night, send nobody rather than someone who arrives after the shut.
